blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Custom Kitchen Cost in Eltham?
blogPosts.excerpt: A complete guide to custom kitchen pricing for Eltham homeowners, including material choices, layout complexity, and what to expect from a local cabinet maker.
body: If you are planning a kitchen renovation in Eltham, one of the first questions on your mind is likely how much it is all going to cost. The truth is, custom kitchen pricing varies significantly depending on the size of your space, the materials you choose, and the level of detail in the design. For a typical Eltham home, whether it is a classic weatherboard or a contemporary build, a fully custom kitchen through a local cabinet maker like Arquette generally starts from around $12,000 for a straightforward layout and can climb to $30,000 or more for a large, highly detailed kitchen with premium timber and stone benchtops. Understanding the key cost drivers helps you budget wisely and avoid surprises throughout your Eltham kitchen project.

The biggest factor in your kitchen cost is cabinetry itself, which typically accounts for 50 to 60 percent of the total budget. At our Eltham workshop, Arquette builds every cabinet from scratch using materials like American oak, blackbutt, or high-grade laminate depending on your preference and budget. Custom cabinetry costs more than off-the-shelf flat-pack options, but the difference is immediately visible in the fit, finish, and longevity. Flat-pack kitchens often warp, chip, or develop alignment issues within a few years, particularly in Melbourne's variable humidity. A custom kitchen built by a qualified cabinet maker in Eltham is an investment that will hold its value and function beautifully for decades, making it a wise choice for homeowners who want lasting quality.

Layout complexity also plays a major role in pricing. An L-shaped kitchen in a standard Eltham home is generally more affordable to fabricate than a large U-shaped kitchen with an island bench, walk-in pantry, or integrated appliance panels. Each additional corner, drawer configuration, or specialty fitting adds to both design time and construction time. If your Eltham kitchen has angled walls, existing structural columns, or unusual ceiling heights, expect your cabinet maker to factor in additional hours for precision measuring and custom jig creation. At Arquette, we provide a fixed, itemised quote before any work begins so you know exactly what you are paying for with no hidden extras or unexpected charges.

Material selection is where you can really control your budget without sacrificing quality. Laminate benchtops and cabinetry doors are the most affordable option, starting from around $800 per linear metre for cabinetry alone. Timber veneer sits in the mid-range, offering the look and feel of solid timber at a lower cost. For Eltham homeowners wanting the ultimate in natural beauty, solid Australian hardwoods like blackbutt or Tasmanian oak are a premium option that adds warmth and character to any kitchen. Benchtop materials, including engineered stone, natural stone, and timber, each carry different price points and maintenance requirements that your Eltham cabinet maker should discuss with you in detail during the planning stage.

Do not forget to budget for installation, which is a separate but essential cost. A professional kitchen installation by an experienced Eltham cabinet maker typically adds 15 to 25 percent on top of the cabinetry cost. This covers delivery, precise on-site assembly, benchtop templating, plumbing connections for sinks, and integration of appliances. At Arquette, our installation team works exclusively with our workshop, which means the people installing your kitchen are the same people who built it. This continuity ensures accountability, reduces miscommunication, and delivers a noticeably superior finish compared to companies that outsource installation to third-party contractors in the Melbourne area.

For Eltham homeowners considering the long-term value of their investment, a custom kitchen typically adds 5 to 10 percent to a property's resale value, according to Melbourne real estate data. In the current Nillumbik market, where median house prices remain strong, a beautifully designed and executed kitchen can be a significant selling point. Beyond resale, the daily enjoyment of a well-designed kitchen, where everything has its place and the workflow feels effortless, is genuinely life-changing. Many of our Eltham clients tell us that their custom kitchen from Arquette is the single best improvement they have made to their home, and that is a sentiment we hear again and again across the Nillumbik region.

The best way to get an accurate cost for your Eltham kitchen is to book a free consultation at our Bridge Street workshop. During this visit, we will measure your space, discuss your design goals, and provide a detailed, fixed-price quote with no hidden extras. Arquette has been building custom kitchens in Eltham for over a decade, and we pride ourselves on transparent pricing and honest advice. Whether your budget is $12,000 or $35,000, we will help you make the most of it. Call us today or visit our Eltham showroom to see samples of our work and discuss your project with an experienced local cabinet maker who understands the unique needs of Eltham homes.

blogPosts.title: The Best Timber for Kitchen Cabinets in Melbourne's North-East
blogPosts.excerpt: A cabinet maker's guide to choosing the ideal timber for your Eltham kitchen, covering durability, appearance, climate considerations, and sustainability.
body: Choosing the right timber for your kitchen cabinets is one of the most important decisions you will make during a renovation, and it is a choice that should be guided by more than just appearance alone. In Melbourne's north-east, including suburbs like Eltham, Greensborough, and Diamond Creek, the climate brings hot, dry summers and cool, damp winters that can cause poorly selected timber to expand, contract, or warp over time. At our Eltham workshop, Arquette has spent years working with a wide range of Australian and imported timbers, and we have developed a deep understanding of which species perform best in local conditions and which ones to approach with caution when crafting kitchen cabinetry.

Australian hardwoods are among the finest cabinet timbers in the world, and they are the most popular choice among our Eltham clients. Blackbutt is a standout option because it is hard-wearing, has a beautiful pale honey tone, and is naturally resistant to shrinking and cracking. Victorian ash is another excellent choice, offering a lighter, more uniform grain that suits contemporary kitchen designs. For homeowners wanting something with more character, Tasmanian oak provides warm, golden tones with a distinctive grain pattern that deepens beautifully over time. These timbers are sustainably harvested from managed forests across Victoria and New South Wales, making them an environmentally responsible choice for your Eltham kitchen renovation project.

If you love the look of rich, dark timber, walnut is an increasingly popular choice for kitchen cabinetry in Eltham, though it does come at a premium price point. American walnut offers a deep chocolate brown colour with flowing grain patterns that add instant sophistication to any kitchen. However, it is a softer timber than blackbutt or Victorian ash, which means it can dent more easily in high-traffic kitchen environments. At Arquette, we often recommend walnut for feature panels or overhead cabinetry rather than base cabinets that cop a lot of daily knocks. This approach gives you the aesthetic impact of walnut while protecting it from excessive wear in your busy Eltham kitchen.

For Eltham homeowners working within a tighter budget, timber veneer over engineered substrates offers the look of solid timber at a fraction of the cost. High-quality timber veneer, typically 0.6mm thick, is applied to stable MDF or particleboard panels, giving you the natural beauty of real wood grain without the price tag of solid timber planks. Veneer is also more dimensionally stable than solid timber, meaning it is less likely to move with seasonal humidity changes in your Eltham home. Modern veneer technologies have come a long way, and when finished with quality polyurethane or lacquer, it is genuinely difficult to distinguish from solid timber in everyday use in a Melbourne kitchen environment.

The finish you apply to your timber cabinets is just as important as the timber itself, particularly in Melbourne's north-east where seasonal temperature swings can stress exposed timber surfaces. At our Eltham workshop, Arquette typically applies a minimum of three coats of premium two-pack polyurethane to all cabinet doors and panels. This provides a durable, moisture-resistant barrier that protects the timber while allowing its natural beauty to show through. For a more natural look, we also offer hardwax oil finishes that penetrate the timber grain and provide a matte, tactile surface. Your Arquette cabinet maker will discuss the best finish options for your specific timber choice and kitchen usage during your design consultation at our Eltham workshop.

Sustainability matters to many Eltham homeowners, and rightly so. When selecting timber for your kitchen, ask your cabinet maker about the chain of custody for their timber supply. At Arquette, we source timber exclusively from suppliers certified by the Forest Stewardship Council or the Australian Forestry Standard, which guarantees the timber comes from legally and sustainably managed forests. Choosing locally sourced Victorian hardwoods over imported tropical timbers also reduces your kitchen's carbon footprint and supports Australian forestry communities. In the Nillumbik shire, where environmental consciousness is part of the community identity, sustainable material choices align perfectly with Eltham's values and add meaningful authenticity to your kitchen project.

The best way to choose your timber is to see and touch it in person. Visit Arquette's Eltham workshop on Bridge Street where we keep an extensive library of timber samples, from pale ash to deep walnut, in various finishes. Our cabinet makers can walk you through the pros and cons of each option in the context of your specific kitchen design, budget, and lifestyle. We will also show you how each timber looks under both natural and artificial light, an important consideration that photographs simply cannot capture. Book your free consultation today and let Eltham's local cabinet making team help you select the perfect timber for a kitchen that will look stunning for decades in your Melbourne north-east home.

blogPosts.title: Built-In Wardrobe Ideas for Eltham's Older Homes
blogPosts.excerpt: Practical wardrobe design solutions for character homes in Eltham, from period-appropriate styling to maximising space in rooms with uneven walls and sloping ceilings.
body: Eltham is renowned for its beautiful collection of older homes, from early twentieth-century weatherboards to mid-century brick veneers and grand Californian bungalows. While these homes have undeniable character and charm, they often come with a common frustration: inadequate wardrobe space. Original bedrooms in many Eltham homes were designed in an era when clothing collections were smaller, and the built-in wardrobes from that period, if they exist at all, lack the internal organisation that modern life demands. At Arquette, our Eltham workshop specialises in designing custom built-in wardrobes that respect the character of older homes while delivering the storage and functionality that contemporary families need.

One of the biggest challenges when designing wardrobes for Eltham's older homes is dealing with walls and ceilings that are not plumb or level. Decades of settlement, along with Melbourne's seasonal ground movement, mean that rooms in many Eltham houses have gently sloping ceilings, bowed walls, or floors that are not quite flat. Off-the-shelf wardrobe systems simply cannot cope with these irregularities and they leave unsightly gaps, do not seal properly, and look like an afterthought. Custom-built wardrobes from Arquette are scribed and fitted to the exact contours of your Eltham bedroom, creating a seamless, built-in appearance that looks like it was always part of the room's original design and period character.

For Eltham homes in heritage conservation areas or with period detailing, it is important that new wardrobe additions complement rather than clash with the home's character. At Arquette, we work with a range of door styles that reference period aesthetics, from classic VJ panel doors that suit weatherboard cottages to clean shaker profiles that complement mid-century designs. Colour matching is equally important, and our Eltham workshop can colour-match your wardrobe doors to existing skirtings, architraves, or ceiling colours so the new installation blends naturally into the room. We can also incorporate period-appropriate hardware like brass knobs or brushed nickel pulls to complete the look of your Eltham heritage home.

Internally, modern wardrobe design offers incredible flexibility that Eltham homeowners with older homes can really benefit from. Custom internal fittings from Arquette include adjustable shelving, pull-out shoe racks, dedicated long and short hanging sections, drawer units with soft-close runners, and integrated LED lighting that activates when you open the door. For smaller bedrooms common in Eltham's older homes, we design slim-profile hanging systems and multi-level shelving that extract every possible centimetre of usable storage. The result is a wardrobe that may look modest from the outside but reveals an impressively organised interior that eliminates the daily frustration of trying to find space for everything.

Sliding doors are an excellent choice for Eltham bedrooms where space is tight and a traditional hinged wardrobe door would obstruct the room's flow. Arquette designs custom sliding wardrobe doors in a range of materials, including timber-framed panels, mirrored doors that visually expand the room, and combination designs that pair mirrors with timber or coloured laminate sections. Sliding doors on quality aluminium tracks operate smoothly and silently, and they are particularly well-suited to Eltham's narrow hallways and compact bedroom layouts. Our team handles everything from initial design through to installation, ensuring the track system is level and the doors glide perfectly for years of daily use in your Eltham home.

Walk-in wardrobes are not just for new homes, and many Eltham homeowners are surprised to learn that an existing bedroom or adjacent space can be converted into a walk-in robe with the right design approach. At Arquette, we have helped numerous Eltham clients transform underused spaces, such as box rooms, wide hallways, or areas behind bedroom doors, into compact walk-in wardrobes with full hanging, shelving, and drawer configurations. The key is smart planning, and our cabinet makers measure every dimension, including power points, window placements, and door swings, to design a walk-in robe that maximises storage without compromising the room's liveability or aesthetic appeal in your Eltham property.

Investing in a custom built-in wardrobe for your Eltham home is one of the most cost-effective improvements you can make, both for daily enjoyment and property value. Real estate agents consistently identify adequate bedroom storage as a top priority for buyers in the Nillumbik market, and a well-designed wardrobe can significantly enhance a room's appeal. At Arquette, we provide detailed, fixed-price quotes for all wardrobe projects, and our free in-home consultation allows us to assess your specific space and needs before any design work begins. If you are in Eltham or the surrounding suburbs and your bedrooms are crying out for better storage, visit our Bridge Street workshop to explore the possibilities with a local cabinet maker who understands your home.

blogPosts.title: Why Custom Bathroom Vanities Beat Flat-Pack in Eltham
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover why Eltham homeowners are choosing custom bathroom vanities from local cabinet makers over flat-pack alternatives, and what to look for in quality joinery.
body: When it comes to bathroom renovations in Eltham, the vanity is often the centrepiece that ties the entire room together. It is also one of the areas where the difference between custom-built and flat-pack is most immediately obvious. Flat-pack vanities from big-box retailers might seem like a bargain upfront, but Eltham homeowners who have taken that route often find themselves replacing the unit within five to ten years due to moisture damage, poor fit, or basic construction that simply cannot handle daily bathroom use. At Arquette, our Eltham workshop builds custom bathroom vanities that are designed to withstand Melbourne's humidity and deliver a premium result that lasts decades.

The primary issue with flat-pack vanities in bathrooms is moisture resistance. Most flat-pack options are constructed from particleboard or low-grade MDF with a thin melamine coating that provides limited protection against water ingress. In a bathroom environment, where steam, splashes, and condensation are daily occurrences, these materials inevitably swell, delaminate, and develop mould around edges and joints. At our Eltham workshop, Arquette constructs bathroom vanities from moisture-resistant substrates and applies multiple coats of waterproof sealant to all exposed edges and surfaces. This attention to moisture protection is something you simply will not find in a flat-pack vanity, and it is the reason our vanities continue to look new years after installation in Eltham bathrooms.

Sizing is another critical advantage of choosing custom. Bathrooms in Eltham's older homes come in every conceivable shape and size, from compact ensuites with odd angles to spacious original bathrooms with generous footprints. Flat-pack vanities come in standard widths, typically 600mm, 750mm, 900mm, or 1200mm, and if your bathroom does not match one of these dimensions exactly, you will either end up with an awkward gap or need to hack the vanity to fit. Arquette builds custom vanities to your precise measurements, whether you need a 730mm unit for a tight ensuite or a 1800mm double vanity for a large family bathroom in your Eltham home. The result is a perfect fit, every single time.

Storage design is where a custom vanity from Arquette truly outshines the flat-pack competition. Generic vanities offer a basic configuration of one or two doors with a shelf inside, which is fine for a rental property but nowhere near sufficient for a family bathroom in Eltham. Our custom vanity designs incorporate deep drawer systems for toiletries, dedicated compartments for hair dryers and styling tools, pull-out bins for laundry hampers, and adjustable shelving that adapts as your needs change over time. Every internal fitting is made from the same quality materials as the exterior, with soft-close mechanisms standard on all drawers. The result is a bathroom vanity that stays organised and functional for your Eltham household's daily routine.

Material and finish options for custom vanities are virtually unlimited compared to flat-pack. At our Eltham workshop, Arquette offers bathroom vanity construction in moisture-resistant plywood, marine-grade timber, and high-pressure laminate in a wide range of colours and textures. You can choose from timber-look finishes that complement Eltham's natural surroundings, clean white or grey laminates for a contemporary aesthetic, or bold coloured panels that make a design statement. Benchtop options include engineered stone, solid surface, and timber, each with distinct advantages for bathroom use. This level of personalisation ensures your vanity integrates perfectly with your bathroom tiles, tapware, and overall design vision rather than looking like an afterthought in your Eltham renovation.

Let us talk about long-term cost, because this is where flat-pack vanities reveal their true expense. While a flat-pack bathroom vanity in Eltham might cost $400 to $800 off the shelf, add another $200 to $500 for professional installation, and factor in the likely replacement cost within eight to twelve years, the lifetime cost becomes considerably higher than a custom alternative. Arquette's custom bathroom vanities typically start from around $2,000 fully installed, and they are built to last twenty years or more with proper care. When you calculate cost per year of service, a custom vanity from Eltham's local cabinet maker delivers substantially better value, superior aesthetics, and a result you will be proud to show guests for years.

If you are renovating your Eltham bathroom and want a vanity that is built to last, designed to fit, and finished to impress, Arquette is your local cabinet maker on Bridge Street. We invite you to visit our Eltham workshop to see and touch our material samples, explore internal fitting options, and discuss your bathroom project with our experienced team. Every vanity we build comes with a detailed 3D design preview, a fixed-price quote with no hidden extras, and a full workmanship warranty. Whether you are updating a single ensuite or renovating multiple bathrooms across your Eltham property, we will deliver a custom vanity solution that exceeds your expectations and stands the test of time in your Melbourne home.
